question: At what age does an infant typically sit without support?
explanation:
• Most infants sit without support by 6-7 months.
• Gross motor milestones are frequently asked in RRB.

question: Apgar score is assessed at:
explanation:
• Apgar is done at 1 and 5 minutes (sometimes 10). Scores 0-10 (heart rate, respiration, tone, reflex, color).
• Score 7-10 = good; 4-6 = moderate; 0-3 = low.

question: DPT vaccine protects against:
explanation:
• DPT = Diphtheria, Pertussis (whooping cough), Tetanus.
• Given at 6, 10, 14 weeks and boosters.

question: Severe dehydration in a child is indicated by:
options: B. Sunken eyes, poor skin turgor, lethargy
explanation:
• Severe dehydration: sunken eyes, very poor skin turgor, lethargy, reduced urine.
• Requires urgent IV rehydration.

question: Kangaroo Mother Care is primarily for:
options: B. Low birth weight / preterm infants
C. Infants with congenital heart disease
explanation:
• KMC: skin-to-skin contact for LBW/preterm—improves thermoregulation, breastfeeding, bonding.
• Recommended by WHO.

question: First vaccine given at birth in India (UIP) is:
explanation:
• At birth: BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B (first dose).
• OPV-0 is optional in some schedules.

question: Normal heart rate range for a newborn (per minute) is:
explanation:
• Newborn heart rate is typically 100-160/min.
• Bradycardia <100; tachycardia >160 in newborn.

question: ORS solution should be:
options: B. Continued with breastfeeding and feeding
C. Replaced by plain water only
explanation:
• ORS is given alongside continued breastfeeding and age-appropriate feeding.
• Prevents and treats dehydration from diarrhea.

question: A child can say 2-3 words with meaning by age:
explanation:
• By 18 months, most children say several words with meaning.
• Language milestones are part of developmental assessment.

question: IMNCI stands for:
options: A. Indian Maternal and Neonatal Care Initiative
B. Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness
C. Immunization and Nutrition Child Initiative
D. Infant Mortality and Nutrition Care India
explanation:
• IMNCI = Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness.
• WHO/UNICEF strategy for managing common childhood illnesses.

question: Child walks alone by approximately:
explanation:
• Most children walk alone by 12-15 months. Crawling ~9 months.
• Denver II / developmental screening.

question: Apgar score of 4-6 at 1 minute indicates:
options: B. Moderately depressed; may need stimulation/supplemental O2
explanation:
• 7-10 good; 4-6 moderately depressed; 0-3 severely depressed.
• Resuscitation per NRP guidelines.

question: Hib vaccine protects against:
explanation:
• Hib prevents Haemophilus influenzae type b (meningitis, pneumonia).
• Given at 6, 10, 14 weeks (with DPT).

question: Mild dehydration: percentage of body weight loss is approximately:
explanation:
• Mild 3-5%; moderate 6-9%; severe ≥10%.
• Clinical signs: skin turgor, fontanelle, urine output.

question: Preterm infant is one born before:
explanation:
• Preterm <37 weeks. Term 37-42 weeks. Post-term >42 weeks.
• LBW <2500g.

question: OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine) is given at:
explanation:
• OPV-0 at birth; OPV at 6, 10, 14 weeks; boosters at 18 months and 5 years.
• IPV also in schedule.

question: Normal respiratory rate for infant (1-12 months) per minute:
explanation:
• Infant 30-60/min. Child 1-5 yr ~20-30. Adult 12-20.
• Tachypnea is key sign of respiratory distress.

question: Pediatric drug dose is often calculated by:
options: B. Body weight or body surface area
explanation:
• Pediatric dosing: mg/kg or per body surface area (BSA).
• Prevents overdose/underdose.

question: Breastfeeding should be initiated within:
explanation:
• WHO: initiate within 1 hour; exclusive breastfeeding 6 months.
• Colostrum is rich in antibodies.

question: Infant doubles birth weight by:
explanation:
• Birth weight doubles by ~5-6 months, triples by 1 year.
• Growth monitoring.

question: Danger signs in sick child (IMNCI) include:
options: B. Unable to drink, convulsions, severe malnutrition, lethargy
explanation:
• Danger signs: unable to drink/breastfeed, convulsions, lethargy, vomiting everything, etc.
• Require referral.

question: Measles vaccine (MR/MMR) first dose at:
explanation:
• MR/MMR first dose 9-12 months; second 16-24 months (UIP).
• Prevents measles, rubella.

question: Neonatal jaundice appearing within 24 hours:
options: B. Consider pathological; investigate (e.g. hemolysis, infection)
explanation:
• Jaundice in first 24 h is pathological until proven otherwise. Physiological after 24-72 h.
• Check bilirubin, blood group.

question: Pneumonia in child: fast breathing for 2-12 months is defined as:
explanation:
• IMCI: fast breathing 2-12 mo ≥50/min; 12-60 mo ≥40/min.
• With cough/difficulty breathing suggests pneumonia.

question: Vitamin K at birth is given to prevent:
explanation:
• Vitamin K prevents hemorrhagic disease (vitamin K deficiency bleeding).
• Single dose at birth (IM or oral per protocol).

question: Developmental milestone: pincer grasp at:
explanation:
• Pincer grasp (thumb and finger) develops around 9-10 months.
• Fine motor milestone.

question: Croup is typically caused by:
explanation:
• Croup: usually viral (parainfluenza). Stridor, barky cough.
• Cool mist, steroids; severe cases need observation.

question: Febrile seizure commonly occurs in age:
explanation:
• Febrile seizures: typically 6 mo–5 yr with fever. Usually benign.
• Rule out meningitis in young or ill child.

question: ORS packet is mixed with:
options: B. Clean water as per packet instruction (e.g. 1 liter)
explanation:
• One ORS packet per correct volume of clean water (e.g. 1 L).
• Wrong dilution can cause electrolyte problems.

question: Low birth weight is less than:
explanation:
• LBW <2500 g. VLBW <1500 g; ELBW <1000 g.
• Risk for morbidity and mortality.
